label: early-sequence (t=3-6) step after a c-initial prefix containing d/k/r
explanation: Sparse feature (0.04% of steps) that fires only at steps t=3-7, in the original phase or on <DEL>, and never in the copy phase. It fires mostly on first occurrences of a token, with the strongest preference for t=4. Rates go up when the first token is c (15x lift, half of the activation mass) and when the previous one or two inputs are d, k or r (6-11x lift). Inputs q/i/o/f and <DEL> are somewhat favoured. The strongest examples look like c ? d k [q] or c ? d d [<DEL>]. No single predicate fits this bag-of-prefix-tokens pattern well. The best one (c-initial, at least two of d/k/r seen, current input not d/k/r) gets dev F1 about 0.21 and mass recall about 0.21. Looser versions reach about 0.5 recall, but precision falls to 2-8%. The feature looks like a weighted conjunction over which early tokens appeared, not a clean concept. It does not fire at t<3, at t>=8, or in the copy phase.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=c (+7.00), prev_tok=k (+4.80), orig0=n (+4.29), prev2_tok=d (+4.22), prev2_tok=r (+4.20), prev2_tok=k (+3.97). Lower it: phase=2 (-6.06), t=7 (-2.84), prev_tok=f (-2.38), prev2_tok=c (-2.21).
